# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

This is a polyfill for the TC39 decimal proposal, implementing (a subset of) IEEE 754 Decimal128 decimal floating-point numbers to provide exact decimal arithmetic in JavaScript. It's a Stage 1 proposal prototype focused on spec compliance over performance (which is not to say that wildly slow code is acceptable).

## Development Commands

- `npm test` - Run all tests with Jest
- `npm run coverage` - Run tests with coverage report (98% line coverage required)
- `npm run lint` - Check code formatting with Prettier
- `npm run format` - Format code with Prettier
- `npm run build` - Build the distribution bundle with esbuild

Before make a git commit, make sure that the project
compiles with `npx tsc`. If that fails, do not commit! Try
to fix the compiler errors first. Also, before to run `npm
run format` before committing to make sure that the code
adheres to our linting practices.

### Running Individual Tests

Jest supports running specific test files:

- `npm test -- tests/Decimal/add.test.js` - Run specific test file
- `npm test -- --testNamePattern="constructor"` - Run tests matching pattern

## Architecture

### Core Files

- `src/Decimal.mts` - Main Decimal128 class implementing all arithmetic, comparison, rounding, and conversion operations
    - Contains an unexported `CoefficientExponent` class that
      represents a coefficient (bigint) and exponent
      representation of the real numbers that actually arise
      in the space of (finite) Decimal128 values

### Key Design Decisions

- Uses an internal coefficient-exponent reporesentation for exact operations
- IEEE 754 Decimal128 model without exposing quantum/precision (no trailing zeros)
- Supports all standard IEEE 754 rounding modes: ceil, floor, trunc, halfEven, halfExpand
- Handles special values: NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, -0
- Finite values have up to 34 significant digits and have an exponent range of -6143 to -6143 to 6144, though for extremely large or extremly small numbers the exponent range goes down to -6176 and 6111, with the understanding that the number of significant digits for such extreme values is less than 34 (subnormal values).
- Does not handle all possible IEEE 754 Decimal128 values: all JS Decimal values are canonicalized at construction (trailing zeroes removed), with the effect that trailing zeroes are not supported
    - Constructing a Decimal from e.g. the strings "1.2" and "1.20" should not be observably different (behave the same)

### Test Structure

- `tests/Decimal/` - Unit tests for all Decimal operations organized by method
- `tests/Rational/` - Tests for internal rational arithmetic
- `tests/dectest/` - Comprehensive IEEE 754 decimal test cases in .decTest format
- Uses jest-light-runner for performance with 98% coverage threshold

### Module System

- ESM modules throughout (package.json `"type": "module"`)
- TypeScript with strict mode targeting ES2020
- Source files use `.mts` extension for TypeScript ESM modules
- Main entry point: `src/Decimal.mjs` (built from `src/Decimal.mts`)

### Code Style

- Prettier configuration: 4 spaces, semicolons, double quotes, trailing commas (ES5)
- TypeScript strict mode enabled
- All source code should maintain spec compliance as top priority

## Important Notes

- This is a prototype for a Stage 1 TC39 proposal, not production-ready
- Spec compliance takes precedence over performance optimization
- The project maintains champion-level quality for TC39 review
- All arithmetic operations must handle the full range of Decimal128 values including edge cases
